name: Pure Hair and Nail Ectodermal Dysplasia
aliases: Isolated Hair and Nail Ectodermal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Congenital hypotrichosis characterized by sparse, brittle, and slow-growing scalp hair
Congenital nail dystrophy including thickened, brittle, or absent nails
Lack of involvement of teeth, sweat glands, or other ectodermal structures
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both congenital hair abnormalities and nail dystrophy with absence of other ectodermal defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by genetic testing when available

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital hypotrichosis with sparse, brittle scalp hair
Congenital nail dystrophy including thickened and brittle nails
searchTerms: thick and brittle nails present at birth
nails that are thickened and break easily

common.symptomName: Nail hypoplasia or partial nail aplasia
Fragile hair shafts prone to breakage

searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
mild palm and foot skin thickening
slight keratin buildup on hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Mild pruritus of affected skin areas

rare.symptomName: Episodic nail infections secondary to dystrophy
searchTerms: nail infections that come and go
repeated nail infections due to damage

rare.symptomName: Transient erythema and scaling of scalp
searchTerms: temporary redness and flaking of scalp
scalp redness with scaling that comes and goes

laboratory: Normal sweat chloride and pilocarpine sweat test
other: Hair shaft microscopy showing pili torti or trichorrhexis nodosa
Nail biopsy showing dystrophic changes without inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Dental anomalies such as hypodontia or conical teeth
Unruly, dry, and frizzy hair that cannot be combed flat

redFlags: Presence of dental anomalies suggesting syndromic ectodermal dysplasia
